nodes.notes: Set severity per IR matrix; open incident ticket; start timeline log.

nodes.label: Scope recipients
nodes.notes: Query mail logs for all recipients of the sender / URL / subject.

nodes.notes: Purge from all mailboxes; block sender domain, URLs and hashes at gateway, proxy and EDR.

nodes.notes: Force password reset; revoke sessions and OAuth tokens; review MFA.

nodes.notes: Isolate affected endpoints, run full scans, reimage if needed, restore access.

nodes.notes: GDPR 72-hour assessment with DPO; notify regulator / affected users if required.

nodes.notes: Update playbook, IOC watchlists and phishing awareness training.

steps.note: Detection & Triage. An employee spots a suspicious email and reports it (report-phishing button or service desk). A SOC analyst triages it — headers, URLs, attachments, sandbox detonation, threat intel — and decides: is it malicious?
Benign path. If it's not malicious, thank the reporter, confirm it's safe and close the ticket. Reporting is never wasted — even false alarms tune detection and reassure users.
Declare the incident. If it IS malicious, the IR Lead declares an incident: set severity from the IR matrix, open the incident ticket and start the timeline log.
Containment. Scope every recipient by querying the mail logs, then purge the message from all mailboxes and block the sender domain, URLs and hashes at the gateway, proxy and EDR.
Eradication & Recovery. Were credentials compromised? If so, force password resets and revoke sessions/tokens, then clean and restore affected hosts — isolate, scan, reimage if needed.
Communications & Regulatory. In parallel, brief management and agree a comms plan. If the incident is reportable, complete the regulatory notification (e.g. GDPR 72-hour assessment) with the DPO.
Close the loop. A post-incident review captures lessons learned — updating the playbook, IOC watchlists and phishing awareness training — and the incident is formally closed.
The full phishing IR flow across five functions: detect → triage → declare → contain → eradicate & recover → communicate → close. Every incident feeds back into stronger detection and training.
